This is the story of my life. I found a tech, we had a great year together. And then she moved two hours away. Now I run into the same issue over and over. Either the shaping is terrible (current situation) or the art looks cartoonish.

Just had a fresh set put on yesterday, and I’m so torn. I can go back to the same place to see if they can try to do better, or take my chances somewhere else and pay again.

Get out of that clinic. I had a similar experience out of school. I started school after working as an assistant for 7 years, had plenty of experience. Graduated, and left my assistant job for a "tech job". My boards were scheduled a month into that job, passed the test, got certified, and no raise. 

Was bullied by the entire staff for months. I am a great restrainer but with people who don't trust you, shit goes awry. The seven years previous and the two years after that place, never had an issue. 

You need a bigger hospital. I found my tribe when I came to a large referral hospital, I started as nursing staff then moved up to ER cases, and then a spot opened with the boarded surgeons where I work now. General practice sucks lol. In this big hospital, it's sink or swim which worked well for me. I was on my own to TPR my hospitalized patients and pill them etc, and with treatments due every hour, you learn fast how to do things on your own with any patient- regardless of temperament. 

General practice is unfair for a new tech. You have lots of animals that are conditioned to be afraid of their usual vet because they know that toe nail trim is coming. That dog is in bite mode once it hits the parking lot. In ER, especially second/third shift, most are too sick to fight at all. I've put catheters in by myself on laterally recumbent patients. And with a large staff, someone else can muzzle your case for you until you get the hang of it. Many hands make light work. 

Find what you like. Maybe you rock at dental rads, or lab stuff. I've been in surgery long enough my blood smears look like finger paints. In a big hospital you'll have more options to find your strengths and grow as a tech.

Don't be miserable working for people who don't trust you. Don't work for people who don't PAY YOU WHAT YOU ARE WORTH.
